images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of LLM2R. (A) Each part is encoded by a shared Point-BERT encoder and compressed by a Q-Former intoKKgeometric tokens. (B) The token blocks of allNNparts are concatenated and followed by the learnable summary block; a causal decoder processes the sequence in a single forward pass, so the summary positions attend to every part, and the key-value cache of the parts processed so far can be reused when further parts are appended. (C) A pose head fuses each part’s states with the summary states and predicts the rotationRRand translation𝐭\mathbf{t}of every part.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison on Breaking Bad. Columns show DGL, Jigsaw, PF++, GARF, LLM2R (ours), and the ground truth. LLM2R recovers globally coherent assemblies whose fragments are placed close to their ground-truth locations, whereas the baselines more often leave fragments displaced or scattered.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on PartNet Table, Lamp, and Chair instances. Columns show RGL, DGL, Score-PA, SPAFormer, Assembler, LLM2R (ours), and the ground truth. LLM2R places parts with accurate poses across diverse object structures, producing complete and well-aligned assemblies where several baselines exhibit misaligned or detached parts.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison on PartNet instances with a large number of parts, such as wire-frame chairs and storage furniture with many drawers. Columns follow Figure4. LLM2R produces coherent assemblies in which the many thin and repeated parts are placed consistently, whereas the baselines frequently yield collapsed or misaligned structures.
